feedback: Evidence: the controller in iteration 2 was identical to iteration 1, so the drop from 69.32 to 54.45 is due to sensor_size 0.012 to 0.016 alone. Oval progress fell from 0.25 to 0.14 and line loss stayed at 1.0 per run. This means the 16 mm footprint is a negative result, and I correct my earlier note that it was confounded: that confound applied only to iteration 0 vs 1. Keep sensor_size at 0.012. Line loss has stayed near 1 per run through every geometry so far (iterations 0, 1 and 2), so the next lever is the sensor offset or span, not footprint. Iteration 0 to 1 showed that widening the span from ±0.024 to ±0.03 m raised the score from 54.37 to 69.32, although that change was also paired with a controller change. Steering oscillation has stayed around 0.13 to 0.15 in every iteration, so it is not yet the limiting factor. Do not expect a result for this candidate from this note. Next race: if progress rises and steering_oscillation stays at or below about 0.15 with y=0.03, keep the offset and test span ±0.04 m as a separate change. If progress falls, revert to y=0.05. If steering_oscillation rises above about 0.15, also revert to y=0.05 before any span change. Keep wheel track, mass and body fixed, because the off-track limit and the evidence do not point to them.
requested_changes: Keep sensor_size at 0.012 m, since iteration 2 shows 0.016 m lowered the score from 69.32 to 54.45 with the controller held fixed.

If progress rises with y=0.03 and steering_oscillation stays at or below about 0.15, keep the offset and test a wider span of about ±0.04 m (sensor x at -0.04, -0.02, 0, 0.02, 0.04), as a separate change.
If progress falls or steering_oscillation rises above about 0.15 with y=0.03, revert the forward offset to y=0.05 m before testing any other geometry change.
